newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank shares down on renewed selling interest.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank shares down on renewed selling interest.

text.p: Shares in Japan's banking sector O#BNK.T weakened in Tokyo on Thursday on renewed selling interest spurred by a growing belief that the shares had already reached their upward limits, brokers said.
As of 0128 GMT, shares in Sakura Bank Ltd was down 13 yen at 796 yen in heavy turnover, while Sumitomo Bank Ltd also off 30 yen at 1,560 yen. Fuji Bank Ltd had dropped 30 yen to 1,500.
Traders said sentiment towards the banking sector was still bearish given the worries about the hefty problem loans held by Japanese financial institutions.

Helping undermine sentiment was Thursday's report by the mass financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun that Japan's top 20 banks are likely to write off a total of five trillion yen of problem loans in the year to March 31.
The banks wrote off problem loans worth some 2.3 trillion yen in the first half of this financial year, after writing off a total of 10.8 trillion yen worth in 1995/96, it said.
Bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
